newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile leader raps "unsuitable" Pinochet remarks.
newsitem.headline: Chile leader raps "unsuitable" Pinochet remarks.

text.p: Chile's civilian president chided former military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet on Monday for criticising plans to abolish eight non-elected Senate seats held by military appointees.
President Eduardo Frei, just back from a high-profile visit to the United States last week, said the military's opinions about his plans to amend the Chilean constitution were not welcome.

"There's going to be an intense political debate about this ... and it strikes me as highly unsuitable for the military to get involved in that debate," Frei told reporters, when asked about Pinochet's remarks.
The 81-year-old former dictator said in a weekend interview that he might like to become a senator-for-life once his term as army commander expires next year.

Under the constitution his own government wrote in 1980, Pinochet has the right to a lifetime seat in the Senate if he wants it. But he said Frei's plans to abolish the lifetime seat and the eight appointed seats were discouraging him.
